sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the northern edge of the Haddonfield business district, a strip of mixed residential and industrial land lying on both sides of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad) where it runs north and south beside North Atlantic Avenue. The sheet is bounded by West and East Redman Avenue at the top and Wilkins Avenue at the bottom, with Westmont Avenue on the west and North Haddon Avenue and Tanner on the east. East and West Euclid Avenue cross the middle of the sheet. West of the railroad the lots facing Westmont Avenue are filled with detached two-storey frame dwellings with small garages, and a row of small brick and concrete-block buildings stands near North Atlantic Avenue. The centre of the sheet is the plant of the Haddon Ice and Coal Company, with engine room, boiler house, ice houses, freezing tanks, a track shed and coal bins served by a wooden trestle and a siding off the railroad; greenhouses stand south of the plant along Turnley Lane. South of East Euclid Avenue the Willets Coal and Lumber Company occupies a large yard of lumber sheds and coal bins with its own curved siding. Below it lie two small residential blocks of dwellings between Rosedale, Allen, Stiles and Tanner, with an apartment building, a filling station and several concrete-block garages near Tanner. Water pipes of the New Jersey Water Company are drawn along the streets, and street widths of 38, 50, 60 and 80 feet are lettered. The block numbers 12, 12A, 84 and 15A are printed, and the adjoining sheets 3, 5, 14, 17 and 22 appear in the blank margins. The scale is 50 feet to an inch, and the sheet is turned slightly clockwise on the page.
notes: Westmont Avenue is drawn 38 feet wide south of West Euclid Avenue and about 60 feet wide north of it; its modern line fits the drawn street only roughly south of Euclid.
Turnley Lane is not a named street in OpenStreetMap; a service way named Veterans Lane follows its line.
Rosedale Avenue is a service way in OpenStreetMap and was not used as control.
Tanner is Tanner Street in OpenStreetMap.
50 ft. One part. Westmont, N. Atlantic, Redman, Euclid, Wilkins, Tanner, N. Haddon; Haddon Ice and Coal, Willets Coal and Lumber. Westmont drawn 38 ft wide south of W. Euclid.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 shows the heart of Haddonfield's business district along Kings Highway East, from the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad) and its passenger station on the west to Chestnut and Tanner Street on the east. Kings Highway East runs across the middle of the sheet and is lined on both sides with stores, offices, banks and apartments, many of them numbered in the 1 to 150 range. North of Kings Highway the blocks between North Atlantic Avenue, Rosedale Avenue, Allen Avenue and Tanner hold dwellings with garages near Wilkins Avenue, and larger premises along the highway: F. R. Tilden Inc. (a cement block works), the parish house, church and rectory of Grace Church Episcopal, the S. J. Dry Cleaning and Dyeing plant with its boiler house, a bowling alley with an entertainment hall beside Tanner, and a group of small greenhouses at the foot of Allen Avenue. South of the highway stand Masonic Temple, the First Presbyterian Church with its manse, two banks, and rows of shops. Below the shops, dwellings front Chestnut, and the south-west corner of the sheet is an athletic field belonging to the school shown on the next sheet. At the left the railroad carries several tracks past the passenger station, with a tunnel under the line marked at the station platforms. The scale is 50 feet to an inch. Water mains of the New Jersey Water Company are marked in the streets, with widths such as 28, 38, 55 and 60 feet lettered, and fire alarm and drinking hydrant symbols appear at several corners. Blocks 12B, 12C, 12D, 13 and 14 are printed, and the neighbouring sheets 2, 4, 5, 6, 17 and 18 are named in the margins.
notes: Kings Highway East and Kings Highway West are East Kings Highway and West Kings Highway in OpenStreetMap; the sheet prints Kings H'wy E. and Kings H'wy W.
Clements Street is Clement Street in OpenStreetMap.
Tanner and Chestnut are Tanner Street and Chestnut Street in OpenStreetMap.
Rosedale Avenue is a service way in OpenStreetMap and was not used as control.
The Allen Avenue and Wilkins Avenue crossing was hand-picked because the detector found no second arm for Allen Avenue.
50 ft. One part. Kings Highway East from the railroad station to Chestnut and Tanner; Wilkins at top. One hand-picked point (Allen/Wilkins).

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the residential district south of Kings Highway, between the railroad and Atlantic Avenue on the west and Center (Centre) Street on the east, with Lincoln Avenue crossing the upper part and East Park Avenue along the bottom edge. Chestnut runs north and south through the middle of the sheet and the sheet is turned a few degrees so that the streets slope on the page. The upper left is occupied by the Haddonfield Public Schools: a large pink brick main building with a frame and concrete-block wing, a separate classroom building and a heating plant, set among open grounds that are labelled Athletic Field and continue onto sheet 3. North of Lincoln Avenue on the east side of Chestnut the lots carry detached dwellings, a few small outbuildings and a concrete-block garage group, and the lots on Center Street, drawn with house numbers in the 50s to 100s, are all dwellings. South of Lincoln Avenue the two blocks numbered 55 and 56 are filled with detached two and two-and-a-half-storey frame dwellings with small garages, and the Community House, a brick building, stands on the east block near Center. A bird house is drawn near East Park Avenue. Along the left edge the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad) runs beside Atlantic Avenue, which is lettered with the alternate name East and South Atlantic. Water mains of the New Jersey Water Company are marked in Lincoln, Chestnut, Center and East Park, and street widths of 40, 55 and 60 feet are given. The scale is 50 feet to an inch. Adjoining sheets 3, 6, 7, 14, 18, 20 and 21 are named in the blank margins.
notes: East Park Avenue is West Park Avenue in OpenStreetMap west of Spruce.
Atlantic Avenue here is East Atlantic Avenue in OpenStreetMap; South Atlantic Avenue is a parallel way about 30 m to the west and was not used.
Center (Centre) is Centre Street in OpenStreetMap; its modern line is about 7 m from the drawn street and it was left out of the control.
Chestnut is Chestnut Street in OpenStreetMap.
50 ft. One part. Lincoln, Chestnut, East Park, E. S. Atlantic; Haddonfield Public Schools, Athletic Field. Four points; Centre Street left out (displaced).

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 lies north-east of the business centre and is only thinly built up. Hopkins Avenue crosses the top of the sheet with a row of detached frame dwellings on its south side, numbered from 120 to 168, and at the east end the Church of the Christ King (Roman Catholic) stands on the corner. North Haddon Avenue and Tanner come together at the left edge, where East Euclid Avenue also meets them, and run south as two diverging streets with a small triangular block between them. In that triangle stands the Haddonfield Library and Historical Society, a cross-shaped building of fireproof construction built in 1917. Further south, between Wilkins Avenue and Clements, are a large frame dwelling and Friends School. Lake runs diagonally across the lower half of the sheet from North Haddon Avenue towards the north-east, with Friends Avenue leaving it to the south, and the Orthodox Friends Meeting House, a brick building, stands east of Friends Avenue near Willits Avenue. In the east is the pottery works of Chas. Wingender and Bros. on the north side of Lake, with dwellings beside it, and a small stream marked Run crosses the upper right corner. The large central part of the sheet is open land in large parcels, numbered block 90 and block 5, with a few scattered dwellings and outbuildings and nothing drawn on most of it. The sheet is turned so that the streets run diagonally across the page, and the scale is 50 feet to an inch. Water pipes of the New Jersey Water Company are drawn along Tanner, North Haddon Avenue, Hopkins, Lake and Clements, and street widths of 45, 55, 56 and 66 feet are lettered. Sheets 2, 3, 6, 8, 9 and 14 are named in the margins.
notes: N. Haddon Av. is North Haddon Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Tanner, Lake and Clements are Tanner Street, Lake Street and Clement Street.
Willits Avenue (Maple) is printed with the alternate name Maple; the index says Maple, see Willits Ave.
The junction of Stiles Avenue and Tanner sits about 3 m off the fit and the Lake Street and North Haddon Avenue junction was left out because it fits less well.
Friends Avenue, Lake Street and North Haddon Avenue form the only control east of Tanner, so the east side of the sheet rests on few points.
50 ft. One part. Hopkins, Lake, North Haddon, Tanner, Stiles; library; mostly open land.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 is the commercial centre of Haddonfield, the blocks around the meeting of Kings Highway East with North and South Haddon Avenue, Mechanic and Tanner. Kings Highway East crosses the sheet from left to right and is drawn about 100 feet wide, lined on both sides with two and three-storey stores with apartments over them. On the north side, between Tanner and Mechanic, stand the N. J. Bell Telephone Company building, the post office, a wholesale tea and coffee store, a large garage for thirty cars and a cluster of frame shops. North Haddon Avenue runs diagonally from the top of the sheet to Kings Highway, with a filling station, a garage, printing and furniture shops, and east of it the fire department with its hose tower, a hall and rows of stores with dwellings above. The First Baptist Church, a brick and concrete-block building, stands south of Kings Highway on the west side, with a general store, a bakery, a hay and feed store and a bank of small garages in the same block. South of Kings Highway the radiating streets are Center (Centre), Ellis and South Haddon Avenue; Ellis and South Haddon Avenue converge toward Snowden and Walnut Avenue at the lower right. The blocks there hold detached frame dwellings, a printing office, a tennis club with its courts, auto repair and painting shops, and a single square building in brown at the right edge. Clements is drawn along the top of the sheet. Street widths of 40, 55, 60 and 66 feet are lettered, and water pipes of the New Jersey Water Company run in the streets. Scale is 50 feet to an inch. Blocks 5, 6, 7, 10, 11 and 13 are numbered, and sheets 3, 4, 5, 7, 9 and 10 are named around the margins.
notes: N. Haddon Av. and S. Haddon Av. are North Haddon Avenue and South Haddon Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Kings Highway East is East Kings Highway in OpenStreetMap; it is drawn about 100 feet wide against 77 feet in the parcels.

Along Kings Highway the drawn distances from Tanner to Mechanic and from North Haddon Avenue to Friends Avenue are about 15 to 20 percent longer than the modern junctions give, so the fit leaves residuals of about 5 m at Mechanic and North Haddon Avenue.

Center (Centre) is Centre Street in OpenStreetMap and was left out of the control. Ellis, South Haddon Avenue, Snowden and Walnut Avenue converge in a tight angle at the lower right and none of their junctions was detected.

50 ft. One part. Kings Highway business centre, North and South Haddon, Mechanic, Ellis. Kings Hwy gaps Tanner-Mechanic and N. Haddon-Friends drawn 15-20 percent long; RMSE 3.8 m, kept as drawn; Centre Street left out.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers a residential district south of the business centre, between Center (Centre) on the west and Park Place (Spruce) on the east, with Lincoln Avenue crossing the middle of the sheet and East Park Avenue along the bottom. Walnut runs north and south through the sheet, and at the top it bends north-east towards Ellis, which crosses the upper right corner with Fowler Avenue joining it. The sheet is turned only slightly, about ten degrees, from the page. North of Lincoln Avenue the blocks on Center and Walnut hold rows of detached frame dwellings with small garages, a Grange Hall, a group of concrete-block garages in rear yards, and the Hicksite Friends Meeting House, a brick building set back in the large block numbered 6 at the top. Along Ellis, in block 9, a mix of dwellings, shops, a cooperative building, an auto repair shop and rows of small block garages stand along the diagonal street front, with dwellings and a few shops numbered from 100 to 190. South of Lincoln Avenue two blocks of dwellings, mostly of two and two-and-a-half storeys with garages behind, face Center, Walnut, East Park Avenue and, at the right, Park Place, where the street bends to the east in a curve. A large building shown in blue (stone or concrete) stands at the right margin. Water pipes of the New Jersey Water Company run in Center, Lincoln Avenue, Walnut and East Park Avenue, and street widths of 30 and 60 feet are lettered. The scale is 50 feet to an inch. Block numbers 6, 9, 10, 51 and 202 appear, and the margins name sheets 4, 6, 10, 21 and 29.
notes: East Park Avenue is West Park Avenue in OpenStreetMap west of Spruce.
Walnut is Walnut Street in OpenStreetMap, and Park Place (Spruce) is Park Place, with Spruce Street as its alternate name on the sheet.
Center (Centre) is Centre Street in OpenStreetMap and was left out of the control.
The junction of Ellis and Fowler Avenue at the top right was not detected.
50 ft. One part. Lincoln, Walnut, East Park blocks, Ellis at top right; turned about 10 degrees. Centre Street left out.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers the western edge of Haddonfield beside Grove, a wide street that curves from the bottom of the sheet north-east to Hopkins Rd. at the top right. At the lower left Lake runs east-north-east and Colonial Av. runs south-east to Willits Av. (Maple) along the foot of the sheet; Glover crosses Grove at the lower right. Hopkins Av. runs along the top of the sheet, with a row of detached dwellings on its south side. The sheet is at 50 ft to an inch and is turned so that north points about 38 degrees to the right of the top of the page. A stream, lettered Run, crosses the middle of the sheet and continues to Boro Park, a public open space beside Silver Lake at the right. Between Lake and Willits are rows of frame dwellings on long narrow lots and several outbuildings, a long shed running diagonally on the west side of Colonial, a work shop and storage building, and a gasoline filling station on Glover with a row of blue-filled garages beside it. A second filling station with tanks stands north of Grove. The blocks are numbered 3A, 3B, 1E and 90, and the neighbouring sheet numbers 5, 9, 15 and 31 are printed in the margins. Pipes of 4 and 6 inches are marked in the streets.
notes: Grove is Grove Street, Lake is Lake Street and Glover is Glover Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Willits Avenue lies about 11 m from its modern line and was left out of the fit; the Grove and Lake junction was also left out because it disagreed with the other Grove points.
The fit rests on three control points and gives a scale 3 percent smaller than the neighbouring sheets.

50 ft. One part. Grove, Lake, Colonial, Glover, Hopkins, Silver Lake; turned about 38 degrees. Three control points (exact fit), scale 3 percent low; low confidence. Willits Avenue (Maple) and Grove/Lake left out as displaced.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 shows the centre of Haddonfield along Kings Hwy E., which crosses the middle of the sheet at 110 ft wide, with Friends Av., Colonial Av., Grove and Evergreen Lane running north from it and Potter running south to Belmont Av. at the bottom. Willits Av. (Maple) runs along the top edge. The sheet is at 50 ft to an inch and is turned so that north points about 35 degrees to the right of the top of the page. North of Kings Hwy E. the blocks hold detached frame dwellings with outbuildings, with a blue-filled row of four stores along the highway at numbers 215 to 221, then The Indian King Club Ho. (built 1750) and more brick-fronted stores. Near the right end stand Artisans Hall and a frame dwelling at the corner of Grove. South of the highway are Boro Hall, a fire-proof, stone-faced building 30 ft high, the large Kingsway Apartments and Haddon Ho., all of brick, with dwellings and garages behind. The south-western part of the sheet holds large tennis courts and open lots with long lot lines. Pipe mains of 4, 6, 8 and 10 inches run through Kings Hwy E. and the cross streets. Neighbouring sheet numbers 5, 6, 8, 10, 17, 29 and 30 are printed in the margins.
notes: Kings Hwy E. is East Kings Highway in OpenStreetMap, and Grove is Grove Street.
Willits Avenue (Maple) lies about 11 m from its modern line and was left out of the fit.
Belmont Avenue is cut by the bottom edge of the sheet; its centre was hand picked from the drawn north edge plus half its width and is the weakest control point of the sheet.
50 ft. One part. Kings Hwy E. centre of town, Colonial, Grove, Potter; turned about 35 degrees. Four points (one hand-picked); Willits, Evergreen, Friends junctions left out (detector on lot lines).

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 covers the district at the north-eastern edge of Haddonfield around Potter Street, with Belmont Avenue across the top and Springfield Avenue across the middle, Prospect Road along the right edge and Fowler Avenue and Snowden (Av.) farther left. The sheet is at 50 ft to an inch and is turned so that north points about 35 degrees to the right of the top of the page. The right half is made of large, partly built blocks of dwellings and auto garages, with Christ M. P. Church (heated by furnace and electrically lit) in the north-east block. On the left, Ellis runs diagonally south-east from Snowden to the junction with Lincoln Avenue, and Lincoln Avenue and Douglas Av. meet in a Y near the foot of the sheet. A greenhouse and tennis courts stand at the top left, and Snowden has a small auto repair shop. Three pink-filled brick buildings, each of two dwellings, stand on the south side of Fowler, and a row of small blue-filled garages and a hall are drawn along Lincoln Avenue. Lincoln Public School, of concrete block with heating, steam and electric lighting, stands at the left. Blocks are numbered 2D, 2F, 2J, 7 and 9, and neighbouring sheets 6, 7, 8, 9, 29 and 30 are printed in the margins. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are drawn in the streets.
notes: Springfield Avenue is Springfield Terrace in OpenStreetMap, and Potter is Potter Street.

The part south-west of Fowler Avenue (Ellis, Lincoln Avenue, Douglas Avenue) has no control points; Ellis Street at Lincoln Avenue lies about 13 m from the drawn junction and Lincoln Avenue was left out of the fit.
Prospect Road is drawn 50 ft wide beside the sheet edge and only its west side is shown.
50 ft. One part. Potter, Belmont, Springfield, Prospect, Ellis, Lincoln diagonal; turned about 35 degrees. South-west diagonal on one hand-picked point; Lincoln at Ellis displaced (13 m).

sheet-11-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 11 fills the lower two-thirds of the page below a heavy dividing line and shows the northern edge of Haddonfield beyond Maple Avenue, at 50 ft to an inch, drawn with Haddon Avenue running up the left side and Marne Avenue across the lower middle. The borough limits follow Haddon Avenue and then turn north-east along the Delaware River Railroad Bridge Company line of the Pennsylvania Railroad, which crosses the upper left of the part, and then along Maple Avenue; beyond them a note refers to the Map of Westmont. Princeton Avenue curves through the middle of the part from Maple Avenue down to Marne Avenue, and Wood Lane curves along the right edge. The blocks, numbered 226, 227 and 228, are a recent residential subdivision of two-storey frame dwellings, each with a small auto garage, on narrow lots numbered 115 to 164 along Marne Avenue and in the 800s along Princeton Avenue. At the corner of Haddon Avenue and Marne Avenue stands a large garage of concrete block and steel frame, with a brick-faced auto show room, a capacity of 25 cars, steam heat and electric light. A small paint shop stands in block 227, and there are a few dwellings of concrete block. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 8 inches are drawn along Haddon Avenue, Marne Avenue and Maple Avenue. The part is drawn turned so that north points about 45 degrees right of the top of the page.
notes: Haddon Avenue here is North Haddon Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
The drawn railroad lies about 17 m from the modern Atlantic City Line against the street fit.

50 ft. Two parts split by a heavy bent line: part 1 (lower two-thirds) Haddon Av, Marne Av, Princeton Av, Wood Lane, Maple Av, Del. River R.R. Bridge Co.; part 2 (top strip) W./E. Elm Av, Westmont Av, N. Atlantic Av, N. Haddon Av, Wayne Av, W.J.&S.S. railroad. Both turned about 45 degrees.

sheet-11-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 11 is the strip across the top of the page above a heavy dividing line, drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned like part 1, so that north points about 45 degrees right of the top of the page. It shows the north-western corner of Haddonfield along the borough limits, which run as a dash-dot line across the top of the strip. West Elm Avenue and East Elm Avenue run along the bottom of the strip, with Westmont Avenue and North Atlantic Avenue rising from them on the left; North Atlantic Avenue and the eastern end of East Elm Avenue are marked as not opened. The large block 225 between Westmont Avenue and North Atlantic Avenue is empty. In the middle the West Jersey and Seashore branch of the Pennsylvania Railroad crosses the strip on several tracks. To its right, block 207A holds six frame dwellings, one of them with a stone first storey and a frame attic, on lots numbered 500 to 524 along North Haddon Avenue, with auto garages, old vacant buildings and a coop behind them. North Haddon Avenue, 66 ft wide, runs up the right side of the strip, where Wayne Avenue leaves it to the east. Water pipes of 4 and 8 inches are drawn along West Elm Avenue and North Haddon Avenue.
notes: West Elm Avenue is Elm Avenue in OpenStreetMap; North Atlantic Avenue and East Elm Avenue are marked not opened.
Placed from two junctions as a helmert; its scale (7.87 px/ft) and rotation (45.7 degrees) agree with part 1 (7.86, 45.2).

50 ft. Two parts split by a heavy bent line: part 1 (lower two-thirds) Haddon Av, Marne Av, Princeton Av, Wood Lane, Maple Av, Del. River R.R. Bridge Co.; part 2 (top strip) W./E. Elm Av, Westmont Av, N. Atlantic Av, N. Haddon Av, Wayne Av, W.J.&S.S. railroad. Both turned about 45 degrees.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 shows the area west of the borough centre where North Atlantic Avenue and the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad cut across the street grid, from West Elm Avenue at the top to West Redman Avenue at the bottom. Westmont Avenue runs down the left side and North Haddon Avenue down the right, with West and East Woodland, West and East Mt. Vernon and West and East Redman Avenues crossing, and the railroad separating the western from the eastern half. The sheet is at 50 ft to an inch, turned so that north points about 45 degrees to the right of the top of the page. The western blocks, numbered 208, 209 and 83, hold detached two-storey frame dwellings with small garages. East of the tracks the use changes: near East Woodland Avenue stand concrete-block garages, an auto repair shop and an auto show room, with an oil house and gasoline tanks, and an auto cleaning building farther south. A railroad station, a switch house and a shed stand beside the tracks near East Mt. Vernon Avenue. North Atlantic Avenue is lettered Not Opened in its upper part and East Elm Avenue is also lettered Not Opened. Rhodes Avenue, Hawthorne Avenue and Merion Avenue are shown at the right margin as stubs of the next sheet, which is numbered 13. Pipes of 4, 6 and 8 inches are drawn in the streets.
notes: West Elm Avenue is Elm Avenue in OpenStreetMap, and West Woodland Avenue is Woodland Avenue.
The railroad is labelled W. J. & S. R. R.; the route is the modern Atlantic City Line.
Rhodes Avenue is Rhoads Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
50 ft. One part. Westmont to N. Haddon, railroad and station in the middle; turned about 45 degrees.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 shows four rectangular residential blocks on the north-eastern side of Haddonfield, between North Haddon Avenue on the west and Wood Lane on the east, and from Ardmore Avenue at the top to Hawthorne Avenue at the bottom, with Wayne Avenue and Rhodes Avenue crossing between. The blocks are numbered 228 to 231. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned so that north points about 45 degrees to the right of the top of the page. Nearly all of it is detached two-storey frame dwellings, many with small auto garages behind, on narrow lots numbered in the 100s along the cross streets. The lots on the west side of the upper blocks are left blank. The one concentrated group is a row of fourteen brick-faced, concrete-block buildings, each 24 ft wide and marked as stores, fronting North Haddon Avenue at numbers 101 to 127 between Rhodes and Hawthorne. A dividing line along the west edge of the sheet is lettered Boro Limits, with the Haddonfield borough line following it beside North Haddon Avenue; the district beyond is shown only as a few street labels (E. Elm Av., E. Woodland Av.) and the neighbouring sheet numbers 11 and 12. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 8 inches are drawn in the streets, with Haddon Avenue at 66 ft and the cross streets at 50 ft. A compass rose stands in the open ground at the right.
notes: Rhodes Avenue is Rhoads Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
North Haddon Avenue is drawn 66 ft wide with the borough boundary along its west side.
East Elm Avenue and East Woodland Avenue appear only as labels at the west margin, outside the borough line.
50 ft. One part. Ardmore, Wayne, Rhodes, Hawthorne between N. Haddon and Wood Lane.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 shows three residential blocks of the north-eastern part of Haddonfield, numbered 232, 233 and 234, bounded on the west by North Haddon Avenue and on the east by Wood Lane. Hawthorne Avenue runs across the top, Merion Avenue and Windsor Avenue cross the middle, and Hopkins Avenue runs along the bottom. The sheet is at 50 ft to an inch and is turned so that north points about 45 degrees to the right of the top of the page. The upper block, between Hawthorne and Merion, holds only a handful of dwellings and auto garages along Hawthorne and a cluster of outbuildings in the middle, the rest of its lots being vacant. The two lower blocks are lined with detached two-storey frame dwellings with small garages behind, on lots numbered in the 100s and 200s. A few lots are filled in pink for brick and blue for concrete block. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 8 inches are drawn along North Haddon Avenue (66 ft) and in the 50 ft cross streets, with fire alarm boxes and hydrants marked at corners. Beyond North Haddon Avenue at the left margin only street labels are shown, East Mt. Vernon Av. and East Redman Av., and the neighbouring sheet numbers 2, 12, 13, 15 and 33 are printed in the blank margins.
notes: North Haddon Avenue is the same name in OpenStreetMap.
East Mt. Vernon Avenue and East Redman Avenue are labelled outside the drawn blocks and are not used in the fit.
50 ft. One part. Hawthorne, Merion, Windsor, Hopkins between N. Haddon and Wood Lane.

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 shows the three northern-most residential blocks of this part of Haddonfield, numbered 235, 236 and 237, between Wood Lane on the west and Grove on the east. Hawthorne Avenue runs across the top of the sheet, with Merion Avenue, Windsor Avenue and Hopkins Avenue below it. On the right the blocks end against Grove, a wide street running north-east, and the streets curve to meet it: Windsor Avenue bends upward and the lots of the lower blocks fan out along the curve. Hopkins Road is lettered at the bottom right where it meets Grove. The sheet is at 50 ft to an inch and is turned so that north points about 45 degrees to the right of the top of the page. The upper-left block, 237, is a large undivided tract with a few buildings, including a brick dwelling with outbuildings, in its middle. The remaining blocks are lined with detached two-storey frame dwellings with auto garages, with lots numbered from the 200s to the 270s along Hawthorne. Water pipes of 6 inches are marked in the 50 ft streets and Grove is drawn 66 ft wide. The neighbouring sheet numbers 14, 8, 31 and 33 are printed in the margins.
notes: Grove is Grove Street in OpenStreetMap.
Windsor Avenue and Hopkins Avenue curve toward Grove; the curved ends were not used as control.
50 ft. One part. Hawthorne to Hopkins between Wood Lane and Grove.

sheet-16.description: Sheet 16 shows the western edge of the built-up part of Haddonfield, a district of detached frame dwellings on either side of Kings Highway West. The upper two thirds is bounded by West Euclid Avenue along the top and Kings Highway West along the bottom. Westland Avenue runs down the middle of the sheet and Estaugh Avenue along the right edge; Peyton Avenue is cut off at the upper left and Avondale Avenue runs down the lower left, where Chews Landing Road leaves Kings Highway diagonally to the south-west. Blocks 49, 50 and 82 are lined with two-storey and two-and-a-half-storey dwellings, mostly with a small auto garage or outbuilding behind, and a few brick dwellings and one cement or stone dwelling are coloured pink and blue. Streets are lettered 80 ft for Euclid, Kings Highway and Avondale, 70 ft for Westland and 45 ft for Estaugh, and New Jersey Water Company mains of 4, 6 and 10 inches are drawn in each. South of Kings Highway the lots front on odd house numbers in the 100s, and a large institutional building coloured blue with a lettered wing stands in an otherwise open block near the bottom of the sheet; a greenhouse is lettered at its right. The large lower left area, blocks 26 and 23, is blank because it belongs to neighbouring sheets, whose numbers (22, 23, 26, 17 and 18) are printed in the margins. The compass rose at the top is turned about 30 degrees clockwise from the page, and the streets run square to the sheet rather than to it. Scale is 50 ft to an inch.
notes: Westland Avenue is West End Avenue in OpenStreetMap (its junctions with Euclid and Kings Highway fit the modern West End Avenue).
Kings Highway West is West Kings Highway in OpenStreetMap; Euclid is West Euclid Avenue.
The fit rests on seven junctions with residuals of 3 to 5 m; the western streets (Peyton, Avondale, Chews Landing Road) do not sit exactly on today's lines, so the part is medium confidence.
The compass rose points about 30 degrees clockwise of the page edge; the fitted rotation is about 31 degrees.
50 ft. One part. W. Euclid, Westland (West End Avenue), Estaugh, Kings Hwy W., Avondale, Chews Landing Rd, Peyton. RMSE 3.5 m, no single street to blame.

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 covers the blocks between West Euclid Avenue, on the north, and Kings Highway West, on the south, from Estaugh Avenue on the left to the railroad and Atlantic Avenue at the right. Linden Avenue runs through the middle and Warwick Road meets Kings Highway West at the foot of the sheet; Westmont Avenue is the street at the right and the railroad of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad) is drawn down the right edge. Blocks 15A and 15B are mostly small lots of detached frame dwellings, two and two-and-a-half storeys, with auto garages behind. The Free Library stands at the upper right on the corner of Westmont Avenue, and the Haddonfield Manor Apartments, a large brick building coloured pink, face Linden Avenue just north of Kings Highway. A large garage coloured blue, with a wing of auto storage bays and a lettered heating and lighting note, fills the lower right block beside the railroad, with smaller commercial buildings against Atlantic Avenue. Street widths are lettered 80 ft for Euclid and Kings Highway, 50 ft for Linden and 45 ft for Estaugh. Water mains of the New Jersey Water Company are drawn in every street. Several adjoining sheet numbers (16, 18, 22, 2 and 3) are printed in the margins where the neighbouring sheets are not drawn. The compass rose at the top is turned about 30 degrees clockwise. The scale is 50 ft to an inch.
notes: Kings Highway West and East are West Kings Highway and East Kings Highway in OpenStreetMap.
The fit uses five junctions at 0.2 m RMSE; Westmont Avenue and the railroad junctions are not used.
50 ft. One part. W. Euclid, Estaugh, Linden, Kings Hwy W., Warwick Rd.

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 covers the south-western approach to the Haddonfield railroad crossing, a district of mixed dwellings, a church and a small factory. Kings Highway West runs along the top; Warwick Road, also lettered Mansion Avenue, crosses the sheet diagonally from the top centre to the lower left, and West Park Avenue and Washington Avenue run across the lower half. Washington Avenue meets West Park Avenue twice, because West Park Avenue jogs where it crosses, and Lincoln Avenue enters from the right at the crossing of the railroad. South Atlantic Avenue and the east side of Atlantic Avenue run beside the multi-track railroad of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad, drawn as parallel lines down the right edge, with a freight station on its west side. The Haddonfield M.E. Church, a large building coloured blue, stands in the middle of the sheet, near Warwick Road. John E. Hand and Son, manufacturers of nautical instruments, occupy a foundry, machine shop and office coloured pink and yellow at the right, with a siding from the railroad. Along the top the lots are small and hold dwellings; below the church the blocks along West Park Avenue are deep lots with frame dwellings. Street widths of 80 ft are lettered on Kings Highway and on Warwick Road, and the mains of the New Jersey Water Company are drawn in the streets. The neighbouring sheets 16, 17, 19, 20, 3 and 4 are printed in the margins. The scale is 50 ft to an inch.
notes: Warwick Road (Mansion Avenue) is Warwick Road in OpenStreetMap.
Washington Avenue meets two OpenStreetMap nodes of West Park Avenue about 37 m apart; both are drawn on the sheet and both are used.
The Lincoln and Washington junction was not detected; the part rests on five junctions.
50 ft. One part. Kings Hwy W., Warwick Rd (Mansion Av), W. Park, Washington, Lincoln; railroad at right edge. Offset crossing Washington/W. Park, both nodes used.

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 covers a regular grid of residential blocks west of Washington Avenue and east of Warwick Road, between West Park Avenue on the north and West Summit Avenue on the south. West Cottage Avenue crosses the middle, between blocks 60 and 61. The blocks are filled with detached frame dwellings, mostly two and two-and-a-half storeys, with an auto garage or small outbuilding behind each; houses on Washington Avenue are numbered in the 200s and 300s. A group of greenhouses is lettered along the rear of block 60 north of West Cottage Avenue, and a pink brick structure stands in the middle of the same block. A row of buildings in block 61, drawn on narrow lots between West Cottage and West Summit Avenues, carries paired dwellings, and two blue-coloured outbuildings stand on its eastern lots. West of Warwick Road the sheet has larger rural lots with scattered dwellings and outbuildings, a barn and sheds, and West Summit Avenue is drawn again at the lower left where it is offset from the eastern stretch. Street widths of 60 ft are lettered on West Park, West Cottage and West Summit and 80 ft on Washington Avenue. The compass rose at the left is turned about 30 degrees, though the streets run nearly square to the sheet. The neighbouring sheets 17, 18, 20 and 26 are printed in the margins. The scale is 50 ft to an inch.
notes: Warwick Road (Mansion Avenue) is Warwick Road in OpenStreetMap.

West Park Avenue is offset where it meets Washington Avenue and West Summit Avenue is offset at Warwick Road; each pair of OpenStreetMap nodes is about 37 to 40 m apart and the sheet draws both offsets.
Six junctions fit at 0.5 m RMSE; two of the offset nodes were not detected.
50 ft. One part. W. Park, W. Cottage, W. Summit, Warwick Rd, Washington. Turned about -5 degrees.

sheet-20.description: Sheet 20 shows both sides of the Haddonfield railroad line south of the station, with Atlantic Avenue on each side. The multi-track railroad of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad) runs top to bottom through the centre and the sheet is turned so that Washington Avenue, at the left, runs obliquely up the page. West of the railroad the blocks 58 and 64 lie between West Park Avenue and West Summit Avenue, with West Cottage Avenue between them, and South Atlantic Avenue runs along the track. Lots there are long and narrow with detached frame dwellings, auto garages behind and a few small tenements along South Atlantic Avenue, and a pink brick pair of dwellings stands near West Summit Avenue. East of the railroad the grid is regular: East Park Avenue, East Cottage Avenue and East Summit Avenue cross between the lettered (East) South Atlantic Avenue and Chestnut, and blocks 57 and 57A are lined with dwellings on both frontages. Street widths of 60 ft are lettered on the Park, Cottage and Summit streets, 80 ft on Washington Avenue and 45 ft on South Atlantic Avenue, and mains of the New Jersey Water Company are drawn in the streets. A fire alarm box stands at Washington Avenue and West Cottage Avenue. The neighbouring sheets 4, 18, 19, 21 and 28 are printed in the margins. The scale is 50 ft to an inch.
notes: East Park Avenue east of the railroad is tagged West Park Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Chestnut is Chestnut Street in OpenStreetMap.
The two sides of Atlantic Avenue are South Atlantic Avenue and East Atlantic Avenue in OpenStreetMap with the railroad between them; junctions on them carry residuals of about 2 m.
50 ft. One part. Both sides of the railroad: Washington, W. Park/Cottage/Summit, S. Atlantic, E. Park/Cottage/Summit, Chestnut.

sheet-21.description: Sheet 21 covers two blocks of the residential district south-east of the Haddonfield business centre, between East Park Avenue on the north and East Summit Avenue on the south, from Chestnut on the west to Walnut on the east. Center (Centre) runs north to south through the middle of the sheet, and Lakeview Avenue and East Cottage Avenue cross between Center and Walnut. The blocks are numbered 52, 53, 53A, 54 and 54A. Nearly every lot holds a detached frame dwelling, most of two storeys, with small frame or concrete-block auto garages behind; two dwellings just south of East Cottage Avenue on the east side of Center are of hollow tile and a third there is of concrete block. Lots front on Park, Lakeview and Cottage with house numbers in the 100s, 200s and 300s. A stand pipe of 110 ft and 400,000 gallons capacity stands on the north side of East Cottage Avenue east of Center, and fire alarm boxes and hydrants are marked at the street corners. Water pipes of the New Jersey Water Company run along every street, from 4 inch mains on Park, Lakeview, Cottage and Summit to 6 and 12 inch mains on Center and Walnut. The blocks are drawn at 50 ft to an inch with the street widths lettered (60 ft for Chestnut, Park and Walnut, 50 ft for Lakeview and Summit). Center Street is drawn wider south of East Cottage Avenue than north of it. The surrounding sheet numbers (4, 7, 20, 28, 29) are printed in the adjoining blocks, which are left blank here. There are no commercial or industrial premises on the sheet, and no churches or schools.
notes: East Park Avenue east of Atlantic Avenue is tagged West Park Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Center is Centre Street in OpenStreetMap; its junctions sat 3 to 7 m off the fit and were left out of the control.
Walnut is Walnut Street in OpenStreetMap.

50 ft. Pilot. E. Park, Lakeview, E. Cottage, E. Summit; Chestnut, Center (Centre), Walnut. One part. Centre Street left out (junctions 3-7 m off; drawn wider south of E. Cottage); Centre/E. Summit jog misdetected.

sheet-22.description: Sheet 22 shows the western residential district of Haddonfield at 100 ft to an inch, a regular grid of blocks laid out between West Elm Avenue near the top and West Euclid Avenue at the bottom. Five north-to-south streets cross it: Peyton Avenue, West End Avenue, Estaugh Avenue, Linden Avenue and Westmont Avenue, with West Woodland Avenue, West Mount Vernon Avenue and West Redman Avenue between West Elm and West Euclid. Truman Avenue and Briarcliff Court run through the lower blocks. The upper half is largely unbuilt, with blocks 217, 218, 220, 222, 223 and 224 drawn empty except for one dwelling at the upper right. Building is concentrated in blocks 211 and 219 at the upper right and in the rows of blocks from West Mount Vernon Avenue southwards, 81, 85, 86, 87, 88, 89, 203, 210, 212 and 213, where small frame dwellings with auto garages face the streets and one row of semi-detached dwellings fills a block on Truman Avenue. A few brick dwellings are coloured pink and several outbuildings are drawn in blue. Street widths of 50, 60 and 80 ft are lettered, and the New Jersey Water Company's four-inch mains run in every street. Fire alarm boxes stand at the upper right and left of centre, and the compass rose is turned about 45 degrees. The neighbouring sheets 11, 12, 2, 16, 17 and 23 are printed in the margins. A date stamp reading July 1929 appears in the oval title.
notes: West Elm Avenue is Elm Avenue and West Woodland Avenue is Woodland Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
24 junctions fit at 0.6 m RMSE; the West End Avenue and West Euclid Avenue junction was not detected.
Truman Avenue and Briarcliff Court are narrow and were left out of the control.
100 ft. One part. Peyton, West End, Estaugh, Linden, Westmont, Elm, Woodland, Mt. Vernon, Redman, Euclid.

sheet-23.description: Sheet 23, at 100 ft to an inch, shows the north-western edge of Haddonfield where the street grid gives way to curving streets, next to the boundary with Haddon Township. Peyton Avenue runs down the right edge and West Woodland Avenue, West Mount Vernon Avenue, West Redman Avenue and West Euclid Avenue cross the right half of the sheet at right angles to it. Avondale Avenue runs down the centre-right on a diagonal; to its left Landsdowne Avenue and Homestead Avenue run down towards West Euclid Avenue and Kings Highway West, and Barberry Lane curves around the junction where West Mount Vernon and West Redman Avenues meet. At the upper left the grid is turned and a second pair of West Redman and West Mount Vernon Avenues cross diagonally, with Homestead Avenue, North Drive and Hinchman Avenue at the edge of the built area. A broken line of the borough limits, lettered Haddon Township, runs diagonally through the upper left and north of the centre. A small stream drawn in blue runs from the top centre into the borough near block 304. The Elizabeth Haddon Public School and its annex, a brick building coloured pink, stand at the right near Peyton Avenue. Dwellings are mostly small frame houses on narrow lots along Avondale Avenue and on the diagonal streets; large blocks 204, 205, 215 and 216 are mostly open. West Elm Avenue and the extension of West Woodland Avenue are lettered Not Opened. Compass and sheet numbers 16, 22, 24 and 26 are printed in the margins.
notes: Landsdowne Avenue is Lansdowne Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Hinchman Avenue is North Hinchman Avenue.
West Elm Avenue and the stretch of West Woodland Avenue east of the stream are lettered Not Opened.
Barberry Lane, the diagonal Redman and Mount Vernon stretches and Hinchman Avenue are not used as control; nine junctions fit at 1.0 m RMSE, none in the upper left.
The streets at the upper left may be sheared from the fit because they have no control points.
100 ft. One part. Curving streets near the Haddon Township line: Peyton, Avondale, Lansdowne, Homestead, W. Euclid, Redman, Mt. Vernon, Woodland. Upper-left diagonal streets have no control.

sheet-24.description: Sheet 24 covers the north-west edge of Haddonfield, the district either side of Kings Highway West where Hinchman Avenue crosses it. The map is drawn at 100 ft to an inch and is turned on the page, with north pointing up and to the right. Homestead Avenue crosses the top of the sheet from the upper left to the right edge, with Barberry Lane joining it from the north-east and North Drive running south-west from it to Kings Highway West. A dash-dot Boro Limits line runs down the left side of the sheet, and the strip beyond it is marked "See Map of Haddon Heights". The blocks, numbered 205A to 205D, 206, 266, 267, 307 and 308, are mostly open lots with few buildings. Below the Homestead Avenue area the sheet is built up only along West Euclid Avenue and Kings Highway West, where a row of detached frame dwellings faces the highway between Hinchman Avenue and the right edge. Dwellings of frame and a few of hollow tile or concrete block stand on large lots on the south side of Kings Highway West, and the largest, a long dwelling with outbuildings, stands in block 206 east of Hinchman Avenue. Loucroft Avenue and Station Avenue cross the lower part of the sheet, and the stub ends of Mansfield Street, Gladstone Avenue, Westminster Avenue and Hinchman Avenue open off Station Avenue at the bottom edge. Several streets carry water mains of the New Jersey Water Company, from 4 inch to 8 inch pipe. Hydrants and a fire alarm box are marked. A block of Hinchman Avenue south of Loucroft Avenue is drawn "Not Open". The neighbouring sheets 23, 25 and 26 are named in the margins.
notes: Hinchman Avenue is North Hinchman Avenue and South Hinchman Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Kings Highway West is West Kings Highway.
W. Euclid Avenue is drawn with a jog at Hinchman Avenue; the west and east parts are offset on the sheet.
Loucroft Avenue meets Hinchman Avenue as Loucroft Road in OpenStreetMap.
North Drive meets Kings Highway West at an angle and its junction sat 4.9 m off the fit, so it was left out of the control.
The Gladstone Avenue and Station Avenue junction (4.8 m) was also left out.
100 ft. One part. NW edge of town: Kings Highway West, Hinchman, Homestead, Euclid; Haddon Heights beyond the left border.

sheet-25-1.description: The main part of sheet 25 covers the south-western corner of Haddonfield on the boundary with Haddon Heights, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned so that north points about 25 degrees right of the top of the page. Station Avenue runs along the top edge. Below it the streets of a large residential subdivision run diagonally across the page: Mansfield (marked not opened), Gladstone Avenue, Westminister Avenue and Queensborough rise to the north-east, crossed by Marquis Road, an unnamed street and Jefferson Avenue; Hinchman Avenue and Hickory Lane cross the upper right, and Chews Landing Road runs from the upper right to the lower left. In the lower half Pomona Avenue, Bellevue Avenue, Clinton Avenue and Chestnut Avenue run north-east, crossed by Oak Avenue and Hutchison Avenue, with Crest Avenue and East High Street at the left edge. The borough limits run down the left side and across the lower part of the page, with the note to see the Map of Haddon Heights beyond them. Most of the blocks, numbered 206, 258, 260 to 265 and 311 to 318, are laid out in lots but still largely empty; scattered frame and concrete-block dwellings with garages stand along Hinchman Avenue, Hickory Lane and Chews Landing Road, several marked as drawn from plans, and long chicken coops stand in block 263. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 8 inches are drawn along the main streets. An inset in the lower right corner, cut off by a heavy line, shows another piece of block 263 on Oak Avenue.
notes: Westminister Avenue is Westminster Avenue, Hutchison Avenue is Hutchinson Avenue, Hinchman Avenue is North Hinchman Avenue and Mansfield is Mansfield Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
A street between Gladstone Avenue and Westminister Avenue is lettered not named.
Several dwellings are marked as drawn from plans.

100 ft. Two parts: part 1 main (Station Av to Oak Av, Haddon Heights boundary); part 2 small inset lower right (block 263 on Oak Av at Clinton Av), drawn turned about 40 degrees against the main part, anchored on one hand-picked point.

sheet-25-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 25 is a small inset in the lower right corner of the page, framed by a heavy line and drawn at 100 ft to an inch, with its own north arrow. It shows part of block 263 on the south side of Oak Avenue at Clinton Avenue, whose names are lettered along its top edge, with water pipes of 4 inches in both streets. The block is drawn turned against the main part of the sheet, with Oak Avenue running almost straight across the top of the inset. It holds two two-storey frame dwellings, a long chicken coop, a garage and two small outbuildings; the lot is divided into three by lot lines. The rest of the block is drawn in the main part of the sheet. The inset carries no other streets, and its placement rests on one hand-picked corner and the scale of the main part.
notes: Placed from one hand-picked point (Clinton Avenue / Oak Avenue) with the main part's scale and a rotation of -14.5 degrees taken from the drawn direction of Oak Avenue; low confidence.

100 ft. Two parts: part 1 main (Station Av to Oak Av, Haddon Heights boundary); part 2 small inset lower right (block 263 on Oak Av at Clinton Av), drawn turned about 40 degrees against the main part, anchored on one hand-picked point.

sheet-26.description: Sheet 26 covers the residential district on the south-west side of the Haddonfield business centre, at 100 ft to an inch and turned on the page so that north points up and to the right. Chews Landing Road (Highland Avenue) crosses the sheet diagonally from the lower left to the top near Kings Highway West, with the blocks numbered 17A, 17B, 255, 256, 257, 258, 62, 62A and 62B laid out on both sides of it and of the parallel streets. A dense grid of narrow lots of detached frame dwellings, each with a garage, lies between Chews Landing Road, West Summit Avenue, Mountwell Avenue, Warwick Road (Mansion Avenue) and Washington Avenue. Jefferson Avenue, Evans Avenue, Hickory Lane and Overhill Road run through the lower left, and Lafayette Avenue and a second street lettered Jefferson Avenue (Lafayette) cross the lower part. A few dwellings of brick or hollow tile and some hydrants, fire alarm boxes and water mains of 4, 6 and 8 inch pipe are marked, together with street widths of 50 to 60 ft. The upper left is mostly open land in block 206, with a pair of large dwellings, farm outbuildings and dashed lines of paths. The upper right, block 16 and block 17, is mostly vacant, with a few dwellings and outbuildings near the Haddonfield title stamp. Kings Highway West runs along the top, with Avondale Road and West End Avenue entering it. Neighbouring sheets 16, 17, 19, 23, 24, 25, 27 and 28 are named in the margins.
notes: Chews Landing Road is lettered with Highland Avenue in brackets, and Warwick Road with Mansion Avenue; the lower Jefferson Avenue is lettered with Lafayette in brackets.

Only Chews Landing Road, West Summit Avenue, Mountwell Avenue, Warwick Road, Washington Avenue and Lafayette Avenue were used as control. Evans Avenue, Jefferson Avenue, Overhill Road, Hickory Lane and Clinton Avenue sat 5 to 8 m off the drawn line today and were left out.
Warwick Road with West Summit Avenue, Mountwell Avenue and Jefferson Avenue has two nearby nodes in OpenStreetMap; the drawn junction is one of them.
100 ft. One part, turned about 30 degrees; Chews Landing Road, Summit, Mountwell, Warwick, Washington. Evans, Jefferson, Overhill, Hickory, Clinton left out (5-8 m off).

sheet-27.description: Sheet 27 covers the southern edge of Haddonfield around Warwick Road (Mansion Avenue), at 100 ft to an inch and turned slightly on the page. Warwick Road runs from the top centre down to the lower left; a Boro Limits line follows it for much of its length and then leaves it south-east of Hutchison Avenue. Haddonfield lies to the east of that line and the land west of it, blocks 259, 263 and 335, is largely vacant. At the top, Hickory Lane and Jefferson Avenue carry rows of detached frame dwellings, with hollow-tile dwellings on Hickory Lane. In the north-west corner Clinton, Bellevue and Chestnut Avenues cross at an angle, and Oak Avenue runs across the left centre. East of Warwick Road a newer subdivision of curving streets is laid out between Heritage Road, Treaty Elms Lane, Gill Road, Glenwood Road, Colonial Ridge Drive and Upland Way, with blocks 320 to 324, 328, 330 and 331. Most of its lots are still unbuilt, apart from scattered dwellings, some of hollow tile or concrete block, and Washington Avenue forms the eastern edge of the part. In the lower left corner, on the Warwick Road side of the borough limits, Hutchison Avenue, Devon Road and Tavistock Boulevard bound block 334, which has several detached dwellings. Street widths of 50 to 60 ft are lettered, and 4, 6 and 8 inch water mains with hydrants are shown. A number of dwellings carry house numbers on Warwick Road in the 400s and 500s. The neighbouring sheets 25, 26 and 28 are named in the margins.

sheet-28.description: Sheet 28 covers the south-eastern edge of the Haddonfield business and residential district, at 100 ft to an inch. The west half is a grid of residential blocks between Washington Avenue on the left and South Atlantic Avenue, drawn with the sheet turned so that north points up and to the right. Detached frame dwellings with garages fill the blocks numbered 63, 63A, 63B and 63C along West Summit, Mountwell, Lafayette and Jefferson Avenues. Further south, between Heritage Road, Treaty Elms Lane, Gill Road and Colonial Ridge Drive, blocks 323, 325, 329, 332 and 333 have a good deal of vacant land and long narrow lots, with South Atlantic Avenue on the right and Greenmount and Hillcrest Drive drawn at the bottom. The railroad, drawn as a bundle of tracks, runs down the middle of the sheet from the top to the bottom edge, with a water tower beside it near the top and sidings drawn to the right. East of the railroad the sheet is mostly open: Chestnut, East Summit and Reillywood Avenues bound blocks 54B and 53B, a pumping station stands south of Reillywood Avenue, a creek crosses blocks 54C and 53C, and Center (Centre) runs south-east down the right side to a vacant block 327 with a few buildings. Block 57B at the top has a row of five frame dwellings facing Chestnut. Street widths of 45 to 60 ft are lettered, and 4 to 12 inch water mains are marked. Neighbouring sheets 20, 21, 26, 27 and 29 are named in the margins.
notes: Chestnut is Chestnut Street and Center (Centre) is Centre Street in OpenStreetMap; Centre Street sat 3 to 7 m off on nearby sheets and was left out of the control.
Treaty Elms Lane is Treaty Elm Lane in OpenStreetMap.
Washington Avenue and West Summit Avenue meet in OpenStreetMap at a point 21 m off the drawn line and the junction was left out.

sheet-29-1.description: The main part of sheet 29 covers the south-eastern blocks of Haddonfield east of Walnut, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, from East Park Avenue south to Reillywood Avenue and the borough water works, and east to the pond on the Cooper River. Walnut runs down the left side; East Park Avenue, Lakeview Avenue, East Cottage Avenue, East Summit Avenue and Reillywood Avenue cross it, and Spruce runs parallel to Walnut in the middle. North of East Park Avenue the U-shaped Park Place and Park Place (Spruce) enter from the top of the page. At the upper right East Park Avenue turns north-east, marked not opened, with Douglass Avenue leaving it, and Berlin Road and Kresson Road meet beside the creek at the top right. The blocks, numbered 52A to 52E, 53B, 53C and 92A to 92E, are thinly built with frame dwellings, many lots still empty. The lower left is a park with a swimming pool, a chlorinator house and a concrete-block bath house, and below it the Municipal Water Works with a brick pumping station, wells, a 300,000 gallon cistern and a watchman's clock. The Cooper River runs down the middle of the page and widens into a pond on the right, with the borough limits along it; Cleveland Boulevard runs south at the lower middle. A heavy line cuts off the lower right of the page, where part 2 of the sheet is drawn.
notes: East Park Avenue between Walnut and Spruce is tagged West Park Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Park Place (Spruce) is the north end of today's Spruce Street; the loop of Park Place was not used as control.

sheet-29-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 29 is the block in the lower right of the page cut off by a heavy line, drawn at 100 ft to an inch at nearly the same rotation as the main part but lying north of it on the ground, around the north end of Douglas Avenue. Lincoln Avenue runs across the top of the part from the left edge and turns north-east, Douglas Avenue runs south-east from it to East Park Avenue (marked not opened) at the bottom, and Ellis runs east from Lincoln Avenue to Potter, which crosses the right side of the part. Park Place curves along the left edge. The blocks, numbered 10, 92 and 201, hold small frame dwellings and a few concrete-block garages on lots numbered in the 200s on Ellis and Douglas Avenue. The Mt. Olivet Baptist Church (colored), heated by furnace with electric light, stands on the south side of Lincoln Avenue, and a second church and a hall stand on Potter near Ellis. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches of the New Jersey Water Company are drawn along Lincoln Avenue, Douglas Avenue, Ellis and Potter. A compass rose sits on the heavy dividing line at the top right.

sheet-30-1.description: The main part of sheet 30 covers the south-east edge of Haddonfield, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned so that north points about 35 degrees right of the top of the page. Kings Highway East, drawn 110 ft wide, runs along the top edge with dwellings, a chapel and a dairy on its south side between Potter and the Methodist Cemetery; at the top right a New Jersey Water Company stand pipe (110 ft elevation, 190,000 gallons) stands beside the cemetery. Lee Avenue, a narrow court of twelve two-storey double dwellings, runs south from Kings Highway. The left half of the part is a residential district laid out along Roberts Avenue, which runs south from Kings Highway and turns south-west at its lower end, with Belmont Avenue, Springfield Avenue (Terrace), Wellington Avenue and Prospect Road; the houses are mostly two-storey frame dwellings with auto garages behind. Below this lies Evans Pond, which fills the middle of the part, with the open blocks 2B, 2C and 2J around it. At the lower left Potter, Park Avenue, Berlin Road and Kresson Road meet just north of the creek that feeds the pond, with a few dwellings, an auto repair shop and the borough limits line. Water pipes of the New Jersey Water Company are drawn along the streets. Two heavy lines cut off the lower right of the page, where two further parts of the sheet are drawn: Kresson Road south of the pond, and Kings Highway East at the Cooper River bridge with Mill Road.
notes: Springfield Avenue (Terrace) is Springfield Terrace in OpenStreetMap.

Potter is Potter Street and Berlin Road is Berlin Road in OpenStreetMap.

sheet-30-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 30 is a block cut off by heavy lines in the lower middle of the page, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned somewhat further than the main part, so that Kresson Road runs diagonally down the part. It shows the area south of Evans Pond where Berlin Road and Kresson Road diverge on their way south-east out of Haddonfield, with Willard Avenue crossing both near the bottom of the page and the short Elmhurst Avenue leaving Kresson Road to the east. A tail of the pond and its creek shows at the top. The blocks, numbered 91, 91A, 92C and 336, hold scattered one- and two-storey frame dwellings with auto garages, a few outbuildings and a laundry of concrete block on the east side of Berlin Road. Lots along Kresson Road and Berlin Road are numbered in the 10s to 100s. A dash-dot line marks the borough limits across block 91A. New Jersey Water Company pipes of 4 inches are drawn along Berlin Road and Kresson Road. Most of the part is open land with few buildings, and the drawing stops at the heavy dividing lines on the right (Mill Road and the Cooper River, part 3) and on the left (the main part).
notes: Drawn about 13 degrees more turned than the main part of the sheet; placed from three junctions (two hand-picked), an exact fit with no check.

sheet-30-3.description: Part 3 of sheet 30 is the strip on the right of the page, cut off by heavy lines, drawn at 100 ft to an inch. It shows Kings Highway East, 110 ft wide, at the top of the part, where it crosses the Cooper River on a bridge at the right edge, and Mill Road, 33 ft wide, running south from the highway towards the lower end of Evans Pond. The Cooper River winds down the right side of the part, with the borough limits drawn along it, and an arm of Evans Pond reaches in at the bottom. The land on either side of Mill Road is open, lettered 2A and 2B, and the only building drawn is a boat house of brick-filled construction near the pond. A north arrow is drawn in the middle of the part. A dash-dot borough limits line also crosses the space above Kings Highway, which is marked as sheet 31. Water pipes of 6 inches run along Kings Highway East. The part has no other streets and one junction, which with the scale and rotation of the main part is all that places it.

sheet-31.description: Sheet 31 covers the northern part of Haddonfield around Silver Lake and Boro Park, at 100 ft to an inch, with the map turned so that north points up and to the right. The top of the sheet shows two blocks of detached frame dwellings: one between Grove, Merion Avenue, Windsor Avenue and Birdwood Avenue (blocks 250 and 251), the other between Birdwood, Hawthorne Avenue and Narberth Avenue (block 253), with block 252 open land to the south. Hopkins Road (Avenue) runs across the sheet below them, and Silver Lake and its arms, drawn in blue with heavy shores, cross the middle of the sheet. A stream coming from the north-east joins the lake near the centre, and the Delaware Township boundary follows a second stream down the right side. Boro Park lies on both sides of the lake and holds a bath house. The lower half of the sheet is a civic district. The J. Fithian Tatem Public School, of brick with hot air heating and electric lights, stands on the left. Evergreen Lane (Reguillah Avenue) runs south-west to north-east along a row of closely built frame dwellings on both sides, with blocks 1D, 1E and 1C around it. Hopkins Road runs south as a straight street through the sheet to Kings Highway East. The Haddonfield Memorial High School, built in 1926 of fire proof construction, with locker, stage, gymnasium and auditorium wings, stands beside an athletic field, and The Bancroft School, a group of institutional buildings with a hospital, stands in block 1A on the right. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 10 inch size are marked and street widths of 50 to 66 ft are lettered. Neighbouring sheets 8, 9, 15, 30, 32 and 33 are named in the margins.
notes: Grove is Grove Street in OpenStreetMap; Windsor, Merion, Birdwood, Hawthorne and Narberth Avenues keep their names.
Hopkins Road (Avenue) as lettered across the top is Hopkins Avenue in OpenStreetMap; the road running south to Kings Highway East has no matching street name there.

sheet-32.description: Sheet 32 covers the north-eastern edge of Haddonfield, between Grove and Narberth Avenue, at 100 ft to an inch and turned so that north points up and to the right. A dash-dot Boro Limits line crosses the upper part of the sheet from the upper left to the right edge, and the ground beyond it is blank. Below the line the streets form a loose grid. Cedar Avenue, East Elm Avenue and Maple Avenue cross the upper left, with block 243 of frame dwellings between Cedar and Grove and block 242 along the borough line. Maple Avenue runs south-east across the middle of the sheet to Bryn Mawr Avenue. Beechwood Avenue runs to the east above it and borders blocks 245, 246 and 247, which have a few scattered dwellings on large lots, and a small stream marked Run crosses block 248 before it leaves at the right edge. Hawthorne Avenue and Merion Avenue run south-east across the lower part of the sheet, with detached frame and brick dwellings on both sides, a few of them of hollow tile, and the Birdwood Club, a large brick clubhouse, is shown beside Birdwood Avenue at the bottom. Narberth Avenue, with its extension Somerset (marked Not Open), runs up the right side to the Cooper River at the lower right corner. At the right edge a Boro Sewage Disposal Plant with filter tanks, an aeration bed, a pump house and a drying house stands outside the borough, and the water along the lower right edge is the Cooper River on the Delaware Township line. Street widths of 50 to 68 ft and 4 and 6 inch water mains are marked. Sheets 31 and 33 are named in the margins.
notes: Rhodes Avenue is Rhoads Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Grove is Grove Street; East Elm Avenue is Elm Avenue.

sheet-33-1.description: The main part of sheet 33 covers the northern residential district of Haddonfield between Wood Lane and Grove, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned so that north points about 45 degrees right of the top of the page. Wood Lane runs down the left edge; Marne Avenue, Ardmore Avenue, Wayne Avenue, Rhodes Avenue and Hawthorne Avenue cross the page from it, curving to meet Maple Avenue, which runs diagonally from the upper left to the right edge, and Merion Avenue curves across the lower middle. Nickolson Lane runs between Wayne Avenue and Rhodes Avenue, Albany Avenue and Marne Avenue rise towards the borough limits at the top, and Cedar and Grove run towards the lower right. The borough limits cross the upper part of the page as a dash-dot line, with a note to see the Map of Westmont and the name Haddon Township beyond; the large block 242 beyond Maple Avenue is empty. The blocks, numbered 237 to 244, 240, 241A, 301 and 302, are filled with two-storey frame dwellings, each with a small auto garage, on lots numbered in the 200s and 300s; several are of concrete block. The Lutheran Church of the Savior, of concrete block, stands on Wayne Avenue at Wood Lane. Water pipes of 6 inches are drawn along most streets. A heavy line cuts off the lower right corner, where part 2 is drawn.
notes: Nickolson Lane is Nicholson Lane and Rhodes Avenue is Rhoads Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
